one_liner: Full-time DC Army National Guard military technician who builds and manages logistics budgets at Joint Base Anacostia-Bolling, in uniform, while serving as a Guard member.
fit_summary: This is a dual-status military technician job that requires DC Army National Guard membership at E-5 to E-7, and nothing on file shows Daniel has military service. It also requires a year of finance and budget experience at the GS-09 level plus knowledge of National Guard budget processes, which Daniel's emergency-management consulting background is not known to cover. Unless Daniel is or will become a Guard NCO with budget experience, this posting is not a realistic target.
eligibility: Limited to current and former uniformed service members (Active, Reserve, Guard) eligible for immediate DC Army National Guard membership; the posting states 'THIS IS NOT A CIVILIAN POSITION.'
Military rank must be E-5/SGT to E-7/SFC, in a compatible assignment, before placement; you must wear the uniform.
One year of specialized finance and budget experience equivalent to GS-09, or a degree in accounting, business, finance, economics, or a related field (submit transcripts if relying on education).
Must have or be able to obtain a Secret clearance within one year of appointment.
Resume must show month/year start and end dates for every job and be no more than two pages.
strategy: Before spending time on this application, confirm whether you have any military service. If you have none, talk to a DC Army National Guard recruiter about enlistment, since membership at E-5 or above is a precondition you cannot meet by applying.

If you are not pursuing Guard service, skip this posting. Look for open-to-public GS-0560/0501 or emergency-management (GS-0089) roles at FEMA or DHS, or Virginia and Northern Virginia local budget or emergency-management jobs, where your IEM experience translates directly.

If you do qualify militarily, write your IEM resume entry around any real budget work. Examples include grant or disaster-recovery cost tracking, client funding estimates, and reimbursement reviews, each with dates and hours per week.
Answer the self-assessment questionnaire conservatively and back each high rating with a specific resume line, because the posting says inflated ratings will be adjusted or excluded.
Do not copy the specialized-experience text; the posting says plagiarism means immediate disqualification. Keep the resume to two pages.
The announcement stays open until 2027-01-21, so there is time to resolve the membership question first.
resume_bullets: Tracked and reconciled [type of funds, e.g., FEMA Public Assistance] costs totaling [$ amount] for [client], preparing [number] reports on obligations and remaining balances; IEM, [mm/yy]–[mm/yy], [hours]/week.
Reviewed [budget estimates/cost projections] against [federal regulation or grant guidance, e.g., 2 CFR 200] and advised [client role] on allowable costs and funding adjustments.
Briefed [audience] on [funding changes/program milestones], translating budget data into recommendations that [describe actual outcome].
interview_questions: Walk us through how you would build and justify an annual budget estimate for a logistics program.
How would you handle a mid-year funding cut that affects program milestones?
Describe your experience with year-end close-out and with reallocating funds before they expire.
How have you explained budgetary regulations to a manager who is not a finance specialist?
watch_outs: Military membership is mandatory, at rank E-5 to E-7; this is not a civilian job, and nothing on file shows Daniel has served.
The specialized experience must be finance and budget work, ideally tied to National Guard or DoD processes; general emergency-management consulting likely will not count.
The job requires a Secret clearance, a uniform, on-site work with no telework, and a commute from Manassas to Joint Base Anacostia-Bolling.
Accepting the position ends any Selected Reserve incentive bonuses, possibly with recoupment of payments already made.
